key_insight: LLMs can mistake more decision-relevant information for sufficient information, even when missing details could still change the conclusion—a failure termed factor coverage bias.
clinical_relevance: In clinical decision support, this bias could contribute to premature conclusions or unnecessary information gathering, including potentially invasive tests.
method: Constructed paired cases with one determinable and one undeterminable decision.
Added a relevant factor to either case without changing its determinability.
Compared relevant-factor additions with irrelevant text additions and tested increased reasoning effort.
evidence_signal: In the controlled benchmark, relevant-factor additions increased selection of the augmented case as determinable despite increased reasoning effort, while irrelevant text reduced selection—an effect substantially reduced by reasoning.
watch_item: The abstract reports controlled benchmark findings, not real-world clinical outcomes, so clinical impact remains unestablished.
paper_title: When to Stop Asking: Factor Coverage Bias and LLM Determinability Judgments with Underspecified Information in Medicine
